L19@P0: Abstract: Open circuit voltage (OCV) is an important characteristic parameter of lithium-ion batteries,
L20@P0: which is used to analyze the changes of electronic energy in electrode materials, and to estimate
L21@P0: battery state of charge (SOC) and manage the battery pack. Therefore, accurate OCV modeling
L22@P0: is a great significance for lithium-ion battery management. In this paper, the characteristics of
L23@P0: high-capacity lithium-ion batteries at different temperatures were considered, and the OCV-SOC
L24@P0: characteristic curves at different temperatures were studied by modeling, exponential, polynomial,
L25@P0: sum of sin functions, and Gaussian model fitting method with pulse test data. The parameters
L26@P0: of fitting OCV-SOC curves by exponential model (n = 2), polynomial model (n = 3~7), sum of
L27@P0: sin functions model (n = 3), and Gaussian model (n = 4) at temperatures of 45 ◦C, 25 ◦C, 0 ◦C,
L28@P0: and −20◦C are obtained, and the errors are analyzed. The experimental results show that the
L29@P0: operating temperature of the battery influences the OCV-SOC characteristic significantly. Therefore,
L30@P0: these factors need to be considered in order to increase the accuracy of the model and improve the
L31@P0: accuracy of battery state estimation.
L32@P0: Keywords: lithium-ion battery; high capacity; polynomial fitting; OCV-SOC characteristics; sate of
L33@P0: charge estimation
L34@P0: 1. Introduction
L35@P0: The battery system is the most prominent energy storage source in electric vehicles (EVs) [1].
L36@P0: Lithium-ion batteries are a promising candidate for EVs due to their high power density, lightweight,
L37@P0: long lifespan, and thermal stability. The use of high-capacity lithium-ion batteries as the battery
L38@P0: system of EVs is the current development trend [2]. To prolong lifespan and increase safety of
L39@P0: the batteries, real-time monitoring of the state of charge (SOC) is indispensable. Since the SOC
L40@P0: cannot be measured directly, many approaches have been proposed to estimate the SOC of the
L41@P0: battery [3–6]. Among them, the model-based method is widely used in the application for its high
L42@P0: accuracy and self-corrective ability [7–9]. These methods commonly used impose or are coupled
